finding: 3705 Barron Way is PIN/APN 164-352-27 in Reno, Washoe County.
Reno GIS identifies the parcel as Industrial Commercial (IC), 5.630983 acres, with Airport Noise Exposure overlay.
Reno Master Plan land-use GIS identifies the parcel as Mixed-Employment (ME).
Reno ward GIS places the parcel in Ward Six, represented by Brandi Anderson.

Reno states that all new data centers require CUP approval and that data-center CUP applications are not being accepted during the moratorium through August 31, 2027 or until adequate regulations are adopted.
A modular compute facility that houses servers or data-processing equipment has material risk of being classified as a data center, regardless of modular packaging.
No site-specific public meeting record was located for 3705 Barron Way, Barron Way modular compute/data center, or PIN 164-352-27; broader Reno data-center meeting and policy records exist.
NV Energy planning materials and TMRPA materials make power availability, customer cost allocation, and clean-energy sourcing central approval issues for data-center-like uses.
TMRPA flags continuous operation, lighting, security, and equipment noise as compatibility issues and notes industrial/commercial areas are more compatible than residential areas.
The easiest path is classification verification now, power/noise/water proof during the moratorium, and a post-moratorium CUP if the use is classified as data center.

The January 15, 2025 Oppidan and Keystone staff packets show Reno staff made data-center CUP support depend on acoustic studies/barriers, generator-use limits, truck-hour and idling restrictions, screening, low-flow fixtures, NV Energy will-serve evidence, and permit-stage utility review.

The February 26, 2025 City Council data-center discussion presented data centers as a broader standards question involving noise, building design, screening, lighting, distance from residents, water, and power; the presentation compared local projects from 7 MW to 28.5 MW against larger regional loads.

Reno's record suggests Barron should not be sold as a generic industrial reuse. The strongest investor strategy is a small phase-one entitlement with explicit MW cap, no-water-cooling commitment, customer-funded utility story, acoustic controls, generator limits, and expansion trigger.

Recommended packet posture is a 1-2 MW phase-one cap, with 3 MW studied as a utility sensitivity and 5 MW+ avoided as a headline request. No site-specific NV Energy feedback has been obtained for 3705 Barron Way; request service screening for 1 MW, 2 MW, and 3 MW before making public power-capacity claims.
